title: Integer overflow in sequence repeat (`str`/`bytes`/`list`/`tuple` `*`) causes heap buffer overflow (memory corruption / crash)
trigger: seq * n sized in unchecked size_t; 8 * 2**61 wraps to 0, so the allocation is empty and the write is not
spatial_evidence: body: 'the allocation is tiny/zero while the write is enormous -> heap buffer overflow'
notes: OPEN at the pin, so no parent build was needed. Reproduces on stock 2e3304a for str, bytes, list and tuple.

title: heap-buffer-overflow: from 0 length int_to_bytes
trigger: int.to_bytes(0, 'big'): the guard is `len < 0`, so length 0 passes and the write is unbounded
spatial_evidence: body: 'the len is 0, thus it pass through if (len < 0)' plus a segfault against CPython's OverflowError
notes: CVE-2024-8948, fix 908ab1ceca15. Fix reversal fails twice over: py/binary.c's mp_binary_set_int now clamps val_sz to dest_sz, so a zero-length destination writes nothing even with the overflow check off, AND the fix is a multi-file commit touching mpz.c, mpz.h, misc.h and objint.c rather than one hunk. The 2023 defect needs the 2023 tree.

title: heap-buffer-overflow: mis-interpretation of float as int at slice_indices
trigger: slice.indices(0.0): a float object is read as an integer, so the read runs 8 bytes past a 16-byte object
spatial_evidence: body gives the object extent [0x7fffef005760,0x7fffef005770) and the access at +0x8 past it
notes: CVE-2023-7158, fix f397a3ec318f. Fix reversal is pointless here: under MICROPY_LONGINT_IMPL_NONE mp_obj_int_get_checked is MP_OBJ_SMALL_INT_VALUE, a shift of the tagged word with no memory read, so the out-of-bounds read cannot occur at all.

title: fun_bc_call: unbounded alloca when heap allocation of VM state fails
trigger: when m_new_obj_var_maybe fails for the VM state, fun_bc_call does not raise -- it falls back to alloca of the same size on the C stack
spatial_evidence: body: 'if m_new_obj_var_maybe fails, it does not raise an exception, but it tries to allocate dozen kilobytes' by alloca; reporter names MICROPY_ENABLE_PYSTACK=0, which is this port's setting
notes: OPEN upstream, so present at the pin and needing no parent build. MEASURED, two arms in one boot: the alloca fallback DOES run with the heap exhausted and is untrapped, and recursion to accumulate allocas stops at depth 8 with a RuntimeError from MicroPython's own mp_cstack_check (MICROPY_STACK_CHECK, 4096-byte margin against MPY_CSTACK_MAX=393216). So a SOFTWARE guard at 393 KB stops the descent while the stack capability's bound sits near 800 KB, and this row cannot demonstrate a hardware stack trap however it is arranged. Recorded as a conclusion, not an open attempt.
